sector_evidence.point: Disability causes catastrophic health expenditure and impoverishment (verified full citation for the draft's claim)
sector_evidence.detail: Yadav J, Tripathi N, Menon GR, Nair S, Singh J, Singh R, et al. 'Measuring the financial impact of disabilities in India (an analysis of national sample survey data)'. PLOS ONE, 2023; DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0292592. Using NSS 76th round data: 57.1% of households faced catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) at a 10% threshold (34.1% at 20%). 19.1% of households that were above the poverty line were pushed below it by disability treatment spending. Out-of-pocket disability spending took about 20.32% of monthly household consumption expenditure. Rural households faced CHE more often than urban ones.
sector_evidence.source_title: Measuring the financial impact of disabilities in India (an analysis of national sample survey data) | PLOS ONE

sector_evidence.point: Certificate access is lower among poorer and less-educated PwDs
sector_evidence.detail: Secondary analysis of NSS 76th round data found the poorest MPCE quintiles less likely to hold a disability certificate, and the chance of holding one rising with education. This is a preprint; use it only for context, and cite NSS 583 for the headline figure.
sector_evidence.source_title: Unidentified Persons With Disabilities in India – A Study Based on 76th Round of NSS (Research Square preprint)

sector_evidence.point: Jharkhand saw a large rise in catastrophic health expenditure
sector_evidence.detail: Between 2004 and 2014, the incidence of CHE rose by 51.3% in Jharkhand.
sector_evidence.source_title: Variations in catastrophic health expenditure across the states of India: 2004 to 2014 (PLOS ONE, 2018)

sector_evidence.point: Disability prevalence is rising in successive NSS rounds
sector_evidence.detail: Rural prevalence rose from 1.8% (36th round, 1981) to 2.3% (76th round, 2018), and the overall rate from 1.6% to 2.2%.
sector_evidence.source_title: Epidemiology of disability and access to disability support and rehabilitation services in India: a secondary data analysis of the NSS (2018) (PMC)

sector_evidence.point: Poverty within Jharkhand is concentrated in rural and tribal districts; Ranchi is relatively better-off overall
sector_evidence.detail: A district-wise analysis of NITI Aayog MPI 2023 data found that Pakur, Sahebganj and West Singhbhum have high MPI values while Ranchi, East Singhbhum and Bokaro do relatively better. Deprivation remains concentrated in rural and tribal areas, which supports focusing on rural blocks such as Angara. This is a secondary journal source; confirm Ranchi's figure in the NITI annex.
sector_evidence.source_title: Multidimensional Poverty in Jharkhand: A District-wise Analysis Based on Secondary Data (IERJ)

policy_context.item: Jharkhand announcement abolishing percentage-based disability categorisation (NEWS REPORT ONLY – no official resolution found)
policy_context.relevance: The Health Minister announced that all PwDs, whether assessed at 10%, 20% or 50%, would fall into a single category. Applications go through the UDID portal, certificates are to be issued within one month, and appeals can be filed within 90 days. No Government of Jharkhand resolution or notification was found, so its scope (for example, whether it overrides the 40% benchmark for the SVNSPY pension or central schemes) is UNVERIFIED. Present it as an announcement, not as settled entitlement.
policy_context.source_title: Jharkhand Becomes First State To Abolish Percentage System For Disability Certificates (The Daily Jagran, 4 Dec 2025)

policy_context.item: Swami Vivekananda Nishakt Swavalamban Protsahan Yojana (SVNSPY): Jharkhand's disability pension scheme
policy_context.relevance: This is the correct scheme name, replacing the draft's 'Jharkhand Universal Pension Scheme'. A 2024 Khunti district release reports Rs 1,000 per month for life, granted on the basis of a disability certificate showing 40% or more disability. This conflicts with the reported abolition of percentage categorisation, so field verification is needed. The scheme is listed on the national myScheme portal.
policy_context.source_title: New hope for people suffering from sickle cell anemia, approval of pension under SVNSPY (Jharkhand State News, June 2024); Swami Vivekananda Nishakta Swavlamban Protsahan Yojana (myScheme, GoI)

policy_context.item: ADIP Scheme (Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances), DEPwD, MoSJE
policy_context.relevance: Running since 1981. Grants-in-aid go to implementing agencies including ALIMCO, National Institutes, CRCs, DDRCs and state corporations, to supply certified assistive devices; corrective surgery is covered where needed. This is the main convergence route for assistive-device camps for Sangathan members.
policy_context.source_title: ADIP | Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD)
